question: Is the terminal preference for a three-turn search teacher's identical-prefix early EndTurn stable under two frozen opponent continuations?
method: Force the teacher-selected short completed turn or longer static completed turn from the same exactly replayed pre-turn state on the first eligible position per independent map. Continue both branches with persistent native three-turn root search and either frozen routed-v6 direct opponent or frozen native two-turn reply-search opponent. All 96 branch games were terminal; action-limit adjudications would have been censored.
interpretation: Early stopping gave a favorable terminal outcome on seven independent maps under at least one continuation policy and a harmful outcome on none of these 24 selected maps. Each individual opponent-policy sign test remains inconclusive at p=0.0625.
Only three favorable maps were shared by both opponent policies. The outcome label still depends on how the opponent continues, even though no strict reversal appeared in this small probe.

Selection conditions on the native teacher choosing an identical-prefix early stop. These results are conditional branch outcomes, not evidence that a learned policy, search teacher or browser bot gained Elo. No student was trained or promoted.
verification: Predeclared protocol b657c8e was pushed before fresh data collection. All 64 teacher-selfplay maps completed. Replayed forced candidate states matched the native exported post-turn observation exactly. Remote one-core nice19 audit exited zero, five focused and 424 full Python tests and Ruff passed; GitHub CI for audit code 026b039 passed.
qualification: Exploratory small conditional terminal-label study on fresh maps. Do not tune or train on these selected positions, quote these conditional signs as an Elo estimate, or infer universal search strength.
